title: Best Dehumidifier for Drying Clothes Indoors (2026)
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for Drying Clothes Indoors
dek: No dryer, no balcony, no problem. With the right setup, a dehumidifier turns a drying rack into a same-afternoon laundry system.
description: The best dehumidifier for drying clothes indoors, plus the setup that dries washing on a rack in about two hours: closed door, fan and continuous mode.
intro: A dehumidifier for drying clothes is one of the most useful appliances a renter or dryer-less household can own. Hang wet washing on a rack in a closed room, and on its own it can take most of a day to dry while fogging the windows and leaving the air clammy. Add a dehumidifier and the equation flips: the machine pulls moisture out of the air, the air pulls moisture out of the fabric, and a load that would have lingered overnight is ready by the afternoon.

It's gentler on fabrics than a hot tumble dryer, it keeps that damp-laundry smell from settling into the room, and it heads off the mildew that comes from drying clothes in still, humid air. The details matter, though — the right mode, a closed door and a little extra airflow can halve your drying time.
We chose these picks from published capacity and airflow specs, manufacturer manuals, ENERGY STAR data and owner reports from people who dry laundry indoors. We don't run our own lab tests.
topPicksLead: The **hOmeLabs HME1003 Wi-Fi** is our top pick for drying clothes, thanks to a high-airflow Turbo mode and a pump that drains through a long session — while the **Midea Cube 20** is the easiest fit for a single apartment room.

blocks.text: The lesson from that test: airflow across the fabric matters about as much as how much water the dehumidifier removes. The two together beat either one alone.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for drying clothes

blocks.text: We prioritized features that speed up drying: high airflow or a Turbo setting, a Continuous mode that doesn't cycle off at a set humidity, and drainage that won't force you to stop mid-load. We compared DOE capacity ratings and manufacturer specs, and matched each model to a realistic room size.

We also read owner reviews from people who use their dehumidifiers mainly for laundry, looking for patterns around noise, tank size and how well units hold up to frequent long sessions. We don't do our own testing.

sections.heading: What to look for in a dehumidifier for clothes

items.label: A Continuous or laundry mode
items.text: Auto modes switch off at a target humidity even while clothes are still wet. Continuous or Turbo keeps working until you turn it off.

items.label: Strong airflow
items.text: More air moving across the rack means faster evaporation. If the unit is modest here, add a fan.

items.label: The right size for the room
items.text: A 20- to 30-pint unit handles a closed bedroom or bathroom; open basements need 50 pints. Check our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/).

items.label: Easy drainage
items.text: A load of laundry can put a lot of water in the tank. A pump, a hose or a large reservoir saves mid-session trips.

items.label: Reasonable noise
items.text: If you'll dry overnight in a living space, look for a quiet or sleep mode, or see our [quiet dehumidifier picks](/best/best-quiet-dehumidifier/).

sections.heading: How to dry washing faster with a dehumidifier

items: **Pick a small room and close the door.** A closed space lets the dehumidifier lower humidity quickly instead of fighting air from the rest of the house.
**Spin clothes well first.** An extra spin cycle removes water the dehumidifier would otherwise have to pull from the air.
**Space items out on the rack.** Leave gaps so air reaches every piece; bunched clothes dry slowly in the middle.
**Set Continuous or Turbo mode,** not Auto, for the drying window.
**Add a fan aimed at the rack.** It's the single biggest speed boost.
**Position the rack near the unit's airflow,** but not blocking its intake or exhaust. Our [placement guide](/guides/where-to-place-a-dehumidifier/) has more tips.
**Switch back to Auto afterward** to hold the room around 45–50%.

blocks.title: Watch the windows
blocks.text: If condensation forms on the glass while clothes dry, the room is too humid for the unit you're running. Close the door tighter, add a fan or step up in capacity. See our guide to [condensation on windows](/guides/dehumidifier-for-condensation-on-windows/).

rows: Keeps the room dry all year

blocks.text: A dehumidifier won't match a dryer for speed, but it's kinder to delicates and workout gear, needs no hookups, and keeps working on the room after laundry day. If you're outfitting a dedicated space, see our [best dehumidifier for laundry room](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-laundry-room/) guide.

A dehumidifier really can replace a dryer for many households, as long as you close the door, use Continuous or Turbo mode and add a fan. The **hOmeLabs HME1003 Wi-Fi** is the best all-around choice for its high airflow and pump drainage, the **Midea Cube 20** is the easiest fit for a single apartment room, the **Shinco SDL-30P** is the budget pick for occasional use, and the **Midea Cube 50** handles open basements and garages.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for drying clothes?
faqs.a: The hOmeLabs HME1003 Wi-Fi, for its high-airflow Turbo mode, 50-pint capacity and built-in pump. For a single small apartment room, the Midea Cube 20 in Continuous mode is easier to live with.

faqs.q: Does a dehumidifier help dry clothes?
faqs.a: Yes. By lowering the room's humidity, it lets wet fabric release water faster. In a closed room, a dehumidifier can dry a typical load in a few hours, and adding a fan can cut that roughly in half.

faqs.q: How long does it take a dehumidifier to dry washing?
faqs.a: In one widely cited magazine test, a dehumidifier alone dried a load in about 4 hours 45 minutes in a closed room. With a fan pointed at the rack, the same load dried in roughly 2 hours.

faqs.q: What setting should I use to dry clothes with a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Use Continuous, Turbo or a dedicated laundry mode while clothes are drying. Auto modes cycle off at the target humidity even though wet clothes keep adding moisture to the air.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for drying clothes indoors?
faqs.a: Match it to the room. A 20- to 30-pint unit handles a closed bedroom, bathroom or small apartment room; a large open basement or great room calls for a 50-pint unit.

faqs.q: Will drying clothes indoors cause mold?
faqs.a: It can without a dehumidifier, because damp laundry pushes room humidity up quickly. Running a dehumidifier during drying keeps the room in a healthy range and prevents mildew. Learn more in [does a dehumidifier help with mold](/guides/does-a-dehumidifier-help-with-mold/).
